newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers unconvinced by prive reversal.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers unconvinced by prive reversal.

text.p: German cocoa traders said on Wednesday consumers were not following the firmer futures market by buying.
"The industry believes this is technical," one said. "As far as buyers are concerned there is plenty of cocoa around and fundamentals are unchanged."

Physical demand remained soft as raw materials for the seasonal chocolate sales peak at Easter (at the end of March) had long been purchased and retail sales did not yet show any fresh impulse after a sluggish picture in 1996.
New York rose to its highest level in four weeks on Tuesday while London was mixed on Wednesday.
Traders here attributed recent short-covering to a large part of March cocoa being in the hands of one large trade house.
One trader said German and Dutch physical bean buyers were extremely passive but British buyers had reportedly been in the market last week when U.S. buyers had also been active.
March cif Ivorian bean sellers were at 2.50 marks/kg and the second quarter price was 2.53.
Cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works were 6.60 marks/kg, basis March, and 6.70 marks, second quarter on a ratio of 2.60.
Sterling was at 2.7542 marks at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday.
